key_insight: A recurrent forecaster’s initial state can serve as a conditioning interface, yielding small accuracy gains without changing backbone weights.
engineering_relevance: Initial-state conditioning offers a lightweight way to adapt recurrent time-series foundation models and inject metadata such as series descriptions.
method: Freeze the xLSTM-based TiRex backbone and train a small head to write context into its initial recurrent state.
Condition the state on spectral summaries or embeddings of text attached to each series.
Compare against static learned states, parameter-matched LoRA, and full fine-tuning.
evidence_signal: Spectral conditioning lowered mean GiftEval MASE by 0.175% with every seed improving; on six MoTime datasets, text conditioning added reductions of 0.15–0.41% of baseline MASE on four datasets.
watch_item: Results are preliminary and TiRex-specific, with small gains that concentrate in mLSTM blocks and are strongest at short context.
paper_title: The Unused Input: The Initial State as a Conditioning Interface for Recurrent TSFMs
